top_news.title: Trump's Family Seeking National Bank Charter
top_news.summary: Donald Trump's family has won preliminary approval to start a national bank, riding a wave of deregulation under the Trump administration. For the president’s family, the goal is to expand the use of USD1, their dollar-backed stablecoin, World Liberty Financial said earlier this month after receiving conditional approval. Bloomberg News Financial Reporter Paige Smith has the details of the move for today's Big Take. (Source: Bloomberg)

top_news.title: Copy Trading Offers Alternative to Traditional Investing
top_news.summary: Steven Wang, Founder & CEO of Dub, launched the copy trading platform 3 years ago after dropping out of Harvard to become an entrepreneur. He says the app offers a unique alternative to sports betting, and fresh opportunities for the increasing number of young Americans who say they are now investing their money to grow try and grow their wealth. Wang says Dub is for great traders who "don't need to go the traditional sort of boys club and Wall Street path to really become the next superstar." (

top_news.title: Canadian Stocks Rise Despite Breakdown in US Trade Talks
top_news.summary: Canadian stocks ended the day higher, thanks largely to gains from precious metals miners, after the collapse of talks with the US unleashed what threatens to become a widening trade war.

top_news.title: Treasury Buybacks Are a 'Cloud' Over Markets, Apollo's Slok Says
top_news.summary: Apollo Chief Economist Torsten Slok comments on the economic impact of the the US Treasury's strategic debt buyback operations. Speaking on "Bloomberg The Close," Slok also discusses the outlook for Federal Reserve monetary policy. (Source: Bloomberg)

top_news.title: Guggenheim's Walsh Says Firm Is Cooperating With Regulators
top_news.summary: Anne Walsh, chief investment officer of Guggenheim Partners, says the asset management firm is fully cooperating with regulators as they investigate an accounting issue at one of its subsidiaries. US prosecutors are looking at Mark Walter's investment empire and his relationship with Guggenheim. Walsh says Guggenheim's investment or trade-allocation processes are not part of the probe. She speaks on "Bloomberg Surveillance." (Source: Bloomberg)

top_news.title: US Expands Search for Critical-Mineral Projects for Defense Gear
top_news.summary: The Trump administration is seeking investment pitches from domestic producers of metals used in fighter jets, night-vision goggles and tank armor.

top_news.title: Tech Leads US Stocks Lower as Nvidia Earnings, Jackson Hole Loom
top_news.summary: Technology names led a decline in US stocks on Monday as investors geared up for a busy week of economic data and earnings from Nvidia Corp.

top_news.title: Nvidia Slides Ahead of Earnings as Tech Stocks Retreat | Closing Bell
top_news.summary: Comprehensive cross-platform coverage of the U.S. market close on Bloomberg Television, Bloomberg Radio, and YouTube with Romaine Bostick, Emily Graffeo, Norah Mulinda and Tim Stenovec. (Source: Bloomberg)

top_news.title: Test Your ETF Knowledge In Our IQ Test
top_news.summary: Bloomberg's Scarlet Fu puts Isabelle Lee, Athanasios Psarofagis, and Eric Balchunas to the test on "Bloomberg ETF IQ" in this week's edition of "IQ Test." (Source: Bloomberg)

top_news.title: First Brands Bankruptcy-Payout Plan Rejected by Federal Judge
top_news.summary: A federal judge rejected the bankruptcy-payout plan of defunct auto-parts maker First Brands, concluding the proposal to raise money by suing a long list of insiders and business partners was not realistic.
